standard_prerequisites.name: Finite presentation is preserved by base change, so the base changed module is still finitely presented
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-base-change-finiteness}, cited at proof lines 4161-4163
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes openness of the flat locus available for the base changed module.

standard_prerequisites.name: The flat locus of a finitely presented module is open
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Theorem \ref{algebra-theorem-openness-flatness}, cited at proof lines 4164-4165
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces finitely many basic open sets covering the closed set cut out by the ideal.

standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness of a flat module is preserved under passing to a sufficiently large index in the colimit
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat}, cited at proof lines 4188-4189
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the localised modules become flat for large enough indices in the system.

core_obligations: Introduce the notation for the base changed rings, ideals and modules (proof lines 4158-4160).
Note that the base changes remain of finite presentation and that the flat locus of the base changed module is open (proof lines 4161-4167).
Cover the closed set defined by the colimit ideal by finitely many basic open sets on which the module is flat, and record flatness of the localisations (proof lines 4167-4174).
Descend the chosen sections and the covering equation to a single ring of the system (proof lines 4175-4187).
Apply the limit-flatness lemma to make the localised modules flat over that ring, concluding the descended condition (proof lines 4188-4193).
proof_roadmap: Base change and openness of the flat locus (proof lines 4158-4174).
Descend the cover to one index (proof lines 4175-4187).
Make the localisations flat at that index (proof lines 4188-4193).
difficulty_reason: The lemma descends a flatness condition on a module at the primes lying over an ideal from a directed colimit of rings to one of the rings in the system. The proof uses openness of the flat locus for a finitely presented module to cover the closed set defined by the ideal by finitely many basic open sets on which the base changed module is flat, then runs the usual finite-presentation chase: the covering equation and the chosen sections descend to some ring of the system, and by the limit-flatness lemma the localised base changed modules become flat for all sufficiently large indices, which puts the required condition in place.
